main_text.p: bitur, quo magis ira deferbuit. Unde maledictus furor Simeonis atque Levi, duorum fratrum, eorumque gladii homicidarum gladii appellantur, quod post aliquot dies in defervescentia affectuum Sichemitas interfecissent. Ut maledicta illa vindicta, quae composita mente concipitur; qua eam sublatam oportuisset. Quo nomine Apostolus Jacobus monuerat, hominem omnem ad iram oportere esse tardum; ac si, ut alibi Seneca, irae maximum remedium sit mora. Non aliud certe remedium, nec ullum efficacius excogitare potuit Theodosius Imperator Christianus. Cum enim irâ praecipiti incitatus, Thessalonicae turbam promiscue occidi jussisset, hortatu religiosissimi antistitis Ambrosii poenitentiam egit, legemque sanxit, ut si quem ad mortem condemnas-fer,Genef.49. v 5. 6.7.Jacob. c. 1.v.19.Putean. Histor. Barbar. libr.1. n. 6. in fin.Ruffin. histor.Eccles. libr.2.c. 18.

page.notes: The bottom catchword "fer," is printed at the foot right, below the last line. The text ends with "condemnas-" at the line end, so the hyphenated word is continued by the catchword. Marginal references are copied as printed, including "49. v 5." and "6.7.", where the v may be a superscript. The Greek reference "Genef." is a printed abbreviation. The printed note "Putean." is a reference to Puteanus. Spelling of the long s is normalised to s throughout.
